clue.text: Idiot husband attracted to old goddess sealing fate

blocks.note: a clot is a fool
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
O is the usual abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A foolish husband is drawn to an ancient goddess who decides people's destinies.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOT + H + O. 'Old goddess' reads as one phrase, but 'old' gives O and the definition is the goddess sealing fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho was one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the spinner who began the thread of each mortal life.

clue.text: Nipper gets caught – something illegally broken?

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
breaking the law is acting illegally

explanation.surface: A young nipper is caught, perhaps after committing some crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' suggests a child, as British slang has it; here it is something that nips or pinches, such as a crab's claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A claw is a pincer on a crab or lobster, literally a part that nips.

clue.text: Speech offering worship putting a daughter off

indicators.note: 'putting ... off' together means setting aside, so those letters are removed from the word
off completes the phrase putting off, meaning the named letters are taken away

blocks.note: adoration is reverent worship
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A sermon offering worship puts off somebody's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: ADORATION loses its opening A and D to leave ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, a grand kind of speech.

clue.text: Priest’s greeting wayward, not right

indicators.note: 'not right' tells the solver one letter standing for right must be left out

blocks.note: a casual greeting
erratic means unpredictable or straying
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers a greeting that goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: HI + ERRATIC with one R taken out gives HIERATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieratic means of or used by priests, as in the cursive priestly script of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: A theologian with hesitation about death, as shown in final notes?

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is one piece of added material

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for death is placed within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is a Doctor of Divinity
the sound of someone hesitating
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A hesitant theologian writes about death in his closing remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The death word goes between the theologian and the hesitation, not around them. DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a crossword favourite for a theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is supplementary material appended at the close of a book or document.

clue.text: Finds very big lake’s behind dance venue

indicators.note: behind says the earlier words follow the dance-venue word in the final order

blocks.note: a nightclub for dancing
V is the usual abbreviation for very
Lake Erie, one of North America's Great Lakes, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone finds an enormous lake lies behind a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finds' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Discoveries are things found, a plural noun matching finds as in archaeological finds.

clue.text: Lord, the old man turning up in a flap

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an earl is a British nobleman
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's elderly father arrives in a state of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' reads as an idiom for agitated; only 'flap' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlap is a flap on a cap that folds down to cover the wearer's ear.

clue.text: Say no to commercial product after end of Christmas month

indicators.note: the product word is attached after the final letter of the month word

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December
a line is a range of goods a company sells

explanation.surface: A shop refuses a product once the festive season is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer is to turn it down or refuse it politely.

clue.text: Saleswoman in eating area by motorway

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, with 1 read as I
a small dining space

explanation.surface: A shop assistant sits in a roadside café beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: MI + DINETTE. The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; the numeral 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian shop girl or seamstress, especially one working in the fashion trade.

clue.text: Wreath made specially with a name on the front

indicators.note: made specially implies the letters are shaped to order, so they are rearranged
these words place the following pieces at the start of the entry

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the usual abbreviation for name
the word itself supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A floral wreath is custom-made with someone's name displayed on the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or chaplet worn on the head, a poetic word for a wreath.

clue.text: Crustacean, a sort confused with fish

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their order

blocks.note: the words themselves supply the letters
a common food fish

explanation.surface: Some kind of shellfish gets mistaken for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracods are tiny crustaceans enclosed in a hinged two-part shell, known as seed shrimps.

clue.text: Mad Parisian, top bod acquiring condemnation

indicators.note: something mad is deranged, so the letters lose their sane order

blocks.note: the words themselves supply all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A deranged Frenchman, a high-ranking type, attracts public censure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bod' is British slang for a person; here it just contributes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Disapprobation is strong moral disapproval, a formal synonym for censure.

clue.text: Put outside theatre or inside?

definitions.note: an example, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: outside says the verb's letters surround the theatre word

blocks.note: to position something is to put it in place
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A question about whether to put something outside the theatre or inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'outside' and 'inside' are examples of the answer, so 'outside' does double duty as signal and as part of the definition's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as inside and outside are prepositions, linking a noun to its position relative to something.

clue.text: Opposing team with angry thought?

definitions.note: past participle: as in a considered opinion

blocks.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a side is a team
seeing red means being angry

explanation.surface: Rival players have some furious ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered means carefully reflected upon, so a considered view is one well pondered.

clue.text: Island nation in which peak always starts to delight everyone

indicators.note: starts to means only the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: a cap is a top or summit
ever means always
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A country where the mountain top always pleases every visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an archipelago republic in the Atlantic off the coast of West Africa.

clue.text: A bit of tin blocking public entrance

indicators.note: something blocking an entrance sits inside it, so the answer lies within the next words

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A scrap of metal is obstructing a doorway used by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' looks like the metal, but it is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is informal for cash, and a cent is a small coin, a little bit of money.

clue.text: Bad act of wise man, imprisoning head monk heartlessly?

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is cut out
imprisoning means locking up, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: a sage is a wise person
an abbot heads a monastery

explanation.surface: A wise man commits a cruel deed by locking up the abbot.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless takes out only the single middle letter of the five-letter monk word, and the result sits after the first letter of the wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or obstruction, a malicious deed done to wreck something.

clue.text: Power shown by lustful man in small vehicle

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
a ram is a randy man, from the male sheep

explanation.surface: A lecherous man flaunts his power from inside a tiny car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small vehicle' suggests a car; it is a baby's carriage. Pram is British for a baby buggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram, short for perambulator, is a little wheeled carriage pushed along with a baby inside.

clue.text: A new coin seen here? One held to be very old

indicators.note: held means gripped inside, so the one-word sits within the coin word

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the usual abbreviation for new
a small coin
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A freshly minted coin is displayed, though it is thought to be antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen here?' is padding for the surface: the coin is imagined as one an archaeologist might dig up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means belonging to the distant past, exceedingly old.

clue.text: Case when number one inhabitant amasses millions

indicators.note: amasses means gathers in, so the earlier letters take in the millions letter

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral for one
a native is a local resident
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A legal case in which the top local resident piles up millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a law case or container; it is the grammatical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The nominative is the grammatical case used for the subject of a verb.

clue.text: One who painted over second entrance

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the painter comes first

blocks.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres, the French Neoclassical painter
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A decorator has painted over a back door.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for the act or means of going in, an entry.

clue.text: See inside enclosed area cut green?

definitions.note: an example, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter is chopped off
inside places the first word within the shortened area word

blocks.note: a courtyard is an enclosed space
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Look inside a walled lawn that has been mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' seems to describe the lawn, but it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is one instance of a colour, alongside red, blue and the rest of the spectrum.

clue.text: Panic? It’s over – go out to get something to eat

indicators.note: go out suggests letters departing from their order and scattering

blocks.note: the words themselves supply all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: The crisis has passed, so someone heads out for a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria sponge is a classic British cake of two sponges sandwiching jam and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is a jam-filled layer cake, so it is food one can eat.

clue.text: Shock report finally appearing in tabloid

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the preceding word
appearing in places the single letter inside the newspaper name

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
its final letter

explanation.surface: A sensational story is finally printed in a popular newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or astonish someone, a verb meaning to shock.

clue.text: Rector, I start with hymn, somehow showing verbal skill

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word that follows
somehow says the letters are combined in some unspecified new order

blocks.note: the words themselves supply the letters
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A vicar says he will open the service with a hymn, displaying his eloquence.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking or writing, a talent with words.

clue.text: Newest info from the French game

blocks.note: la is French for the, feminine
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Up-to-date news comes in from a French match.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest, used as a noun, is the most recent news or update on a story.

clue.text: To be gripping not everyone, one put in power

indicators.note: not tells the solver to take away the letters for the following word

blocks.note: to enthral is to grip an audience
all means everyone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holding the attention of only some people, one person is installed as ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTHRAL minus ALL leaves ENTHR, then ONE is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthrone a monarch or bishop is to install them formally on a throne with authority.

clue.text: Energy’s associated with enzyme

blocks.note: pep is energy, with the possessive s
being in with someone means being associated with them

explanation.surface: Vitality is linked to a particular digestive chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsin is the digestive protein found in the stomach that breaks down proteins.
